blocks.text: A class should distinguish operations that observe an object from those that change it. int x() const places const after the parameter list to declare that this query does not modify the point's state. It can be called on either a modifiable Punto or a const Punto. mover_a changes the coordinates and is not declared const.

const on a variable indicates that the object must not be changed through ordinary operations. const on a member function specifies how the operation can be used on the object on which it is called. These are different positions with related purposes.

blocks.question: Why is that call rejected even though the numbers are small?
options: const only prevents reassigning the entire object; its members remain modifiable.
The values are in the domain, so modification of a const object must be allowed.

blocks.text: Adding const to an object's declaration does not choose a numeric result or automatically copy its state. The object is initialized as written; const restricts which modifications are permitted afterward.
A const Query Also Constrains Its Implementation

Copy the original dimension into a const object and show that the copy keeps its values after you modify the original.

Criteria: const queries allow reading constant objects and references, do not change their members, and preserve the requested format; cambiar_a remains a modifying operation; a copy is independent and retains its state at the moment it was made.
